issue.body:
## Bug

On macOS, invoking the native **View → Toggle Developer Tools** command (or its `Cmd+Option+I` accelerator) can throw an uncaught exception in Electron's main process instead of opening DevTools.

The reporter sees the standard “A JavaScript error occurred in the main process” dialog with:

```text
Uncaught Exception:
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toggleDevTools')
    at webContentsMethod (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:31239)
    at Object.execute (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:28651)
    at MenuItem.click (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:35249)
    at a._executeCommand (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:40710)
```

![macOS main-process error after toggling DevTools](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-macos-toggle-devtools-crash-20260823/.issue-assets/macos-toggle-devtools-crash-20260823/devtools-crash.png)

**Source:** Direct Codex report on 2026-08-23 (no public chat URL)  
**Reported by:** @illegalcall  
**First observed:** 2026-08-23 on a nightly build; exact regression onset is not established  
**Analyzed against:** `c86b58d04a38ce669be3215ab0834e29cf2c0d30` (`origin/main`)  
**AO desktop version:** `0.12.7-nightly.202608181938` (bundled daemon reports `dev`, healthy on port `3001`)  
**Environment:** macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), Apple Silicon (`arm64`)  
**Priority:** P2 — the action crashes the Electron main process, but the scope is bounded to the native DevTools command and an in-app DevTools path is available  
**Confidence:** High — the stack, platform menu setup, and exact failing mechanism have been traced; an existing tested PR implements the same fix

## Reproduction

1. Launch Agent Orchestrator on macOS.
2. Focus a surface backed by a `WebContentsView` (the Browser panel is the common case).
3. Choose **View → Toggle Developer Tools** from the native macOS application menu, or press `Cmd+Option+I`.
4. Observe the uncaught `toggleDevTools` exception and main-process error dialog.

## Expected

DevTools opens for the focused AO surface, or the shell surface as a safe fallback, without terminating the main process.

## Actual

Electron's native menu command attempts to call `toggleDevTools` through an undefined focused-window target and throws an uncaught exception in the main process.

## Root Cause

`frontend/src/main.ts` installs AO's guarded application menu only on Windows. On macOS, Electron's default application menu remains active, including the built-in `role: "toggleDevTools"` command.

AO composes its window from a `BaseWindow` and `WebContentsView` surfaces. When focus belongs to a `WebContentsView`, Electron's built-in role resolves no focused `BrowserWindow`, then its internal `webContentsMethod` path attempts to access `toggleDevTools` on an undefined target. This matches the `MenuItem.click` stack in the report.

AO's custom titlebar IPC handler and Windows menu already route DevTools through guarded AO logic; the native default macOS menu is the unguarded path.

## Suggested Fix

Install an explicit macOS application menu and replace only the built-in DevTools role with a click handler that:

1. toggles DevTools for the last-focused AO browser surface; and
2. falls back to the shell `webContents` when no browser surface is available.

Keep the standard macOS app roles (About, Services, Hide, Hide Others, Show All, Quit) when replacing Electron's default menu.

## Impact

- A standard macOS menu item and accelerator can crash the Electron main process.
- No data loss was observed in this report.
- Workaround: avoid the native menu/accelerator and use AO's in-app DevTools control where available.

## Related

- [PR #3910](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3910) — open, tested implementation of the traced fix; awaiting review and currently has no closing issue reference.
